evidence: Frozen task .qc-cache/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r3/task (input d622da81...). (1) tests/scoring.toml (sha256 95f70d6e...) is byte-identical to the frozen template rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/scoring.toml: [gates] render=0.0, constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2 (sum 1.0); [floors] functional=0.05; every name has a directory (tests/gates/{render,constraints}, tests/scored/{functional,polish,visual}). (2) All five judge.toml headers match the template except for one added comment line ('# Criterion weights: 1.0 standard, 1.5 important, 2.0 core to the brief (Visual Likert rows are equal).'). Each has [judge] judge='claude-code', mode='batched', isolated=false and prompt_template='prompt.md'. Timeouts are 600 for render and constraints, 9000 for functional and 900 for polish and visual. No file sets model, reasoning_effort, temperature or [judge].weight. Every file has the playwright stdio server (playwright-mcp --headless --isolated --executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium --no-sandbox). Only scored/functional/judge.toml adds [[judge.mcp_servers]] name='verifier', command='/usr/local/bin/python3', args=['/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py', '$APP_RESTART_HELPER']. Gates use aggregation='all_pass' and scored dimensions use 'weighted_mean'. (3) tests/test.sh, tests/tools/score.py, tests/tools/restart_mcp.py and tests/Dockerfile are byte-identical to the template (diff empty). test.sh:191-193 does chmod 755 on the generated helper, removes the .used marker and runs 'export APP_RESTART_HELPER="$LOG_DIR/app-restart.sh"'. That happens before run_suite gates (test.sh:213) and run_suite scored (test.sh:223). test.sh:195-201 substitutes {app_context} into every tests/*/*/prompt.md. restart_mcp.py:9 reads the helper from argv[1], and restart_mcp.py:14 exposes the single-use 'restart_app' tool. The functional prompt calls restart_app once, at the end (line 1 and protocol D, line 59). No other prompt mentions restart. tests/Dockerfile pins harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7 and @playwright/mcp@0.0.79, uses python:3.12-slim (so /usr/local/bin/python3 exists) and symlinks /usr/local/bin/chromium. (4) Criteria (tomllib parse): render has 1 binary criterion (hro_gate_render) and constraints has 1 binary (hro_gate_shared), so both gates are binary. Functional has 44 binary (weights 1:21, 1.5:12, 2:11), polish 5 binary (2:4, 1.5:1) and visual 5 likert with points=5 and weight 1. Ids and names are unique per file and match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ (RewardKit models.py _SAFE_NAME_RE). Descriptions are non-empty. No criterion has keys beyond id/name/type/weight/description/points. All files are LF, with no CRLF. (5) Prompts resolve: each prompt_template 'prompt.md' exists, contains {criteria} and {app_context}, and opens http://localhost:3000. The functional and polish prompts also contain the literal '{ triggerOk, met, ms }' (functional prompt.md:21, polish prompt.md:18). I checked this against the pinned RewardKit source. harbor-rewardkit 0.1.7 judges.py:133 renders with tmpl.replace('{criteria}', ...) and test.sh uses str.replace for {app_context}. Neither uses str.format, so the stray braces are safe. (6) MEASURED: I downloaded the pinned wheel harbor_rewardkit-0.1.7 (sha256 cb9938e5...) to the scratchpad and ran rewardkit.runner.discover() on a scratch copy of the frozen tests/gates and tests/scored (litellm stubbed, Windows Python 3.12, pydantic 2.13.5). It built 5 AgentJudge rewards with no error. gates/constraints and gates/render: all_pass, 1 Binary each, timeout 600. scored/functional: weighted_mean, 44 Binary, weights {1.0, 1.5, 2.0}, MCP servers [playwright, verifier (/usr/local/bin/python3 /tests/tools/restart_mcp.py $APP_RESTART_HELPER)], timeout 9000. polish: 5 Binary. visual: 5 Likert5. Every system_prompt contains {criteria}. The integer TOML weights (weight = 1 / 2, where the template writes 1.0/2.0) were coerced to float. RewardKit agents.py:66 applies os.path.expandvars to MCP args, which resolves the exported $APP_RESTART_HELPER. The output is saved at qc/runs/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r3/per-row-review/evidence/24/rewardkit_discover.txt. (7) Budget nesting (supporting): gate judges 600 < 1500 gate budget; functional+polish+visual 9000+900+900=10800 < 11100 scored budget (--max-concurrent-agent 1); 1500+11100=12600 < [verifier].timeout_sec 13200 (task.toml:27). Colderwater lessons checked against this row: L2, one documented weight scheme: yes, 1.0/1.5/2.0 is commented in every judge.toml and the dimension weights are untouched. L4, simple gates: yes, the render gate is a sign-in; the constraints gate is one server-backed add, a reload and an independent-context readback; both are binary and all_pass. L10, prompt size: the largest assembled prompt (functional prompt.md with app_context substituted, plus all of judge.toml) is about 51,254 bytes, under 128 KB. L13: every prompt uses localhost only. L11 (infra crashes): no run export exists to inspect. Not exercised (does not change the structural verdict): no configured RewardKit or judge run in the Linux verifier image. So 'claude mcp add' registration, the live MCP launch and the restart_app call inside RewardKit were not observed; the raw-evidence-index scope says full configured grading is absent. Adversarial probes: a broken app cannot exploit this wiring (gates zero the reward before scored; score.py is template-identical). A conforming app is not failed by the structure, because both prompt placeholders resolve and the restart server is wired.
run_verdict: PARTIAL (RewardKit 0.1.7 discovery and parsing of all five judge.toml files measured locally; a live configured verifier run with MCP registration and restart_app not exercised)
